name: Peng Zhongxi
profile: Listed on the Hurun China Rich List (2010) as Peng Zhongxi (彭忠喜), wealth from Jindadi Materials (cement). No English or Chinese web sources found confirming his current role or company details.
notes: Very low web footprint; only appeared on Hurun 2010. Would need Chinese corporate registry (Qichacha/Tianyancha) checks to confirm company and role.

name: Chen Guorong
current_role: Chairman (as of 2004 source), Wenzhou Dongyi Shoe Industry Co. (温州东艺鞋业); current status unverified
profile: Wenzhou footwear entrepreneur (陈国荣), chairman of Dongyi Shoes and a former vice-president of the Wenzhou Federation of Industry and Commerce. Listed on the Hurun China Rich List in 2008. No recent public information found on his current activities.
interesting_fact: Dongyi was reported as a major Wenzhou leather-shoe supplier to US retailer Payless, shipping around one million pairs a year from 2002.
deep_cut_fact: In Dec 2004 he spoke at a Chinese Foreign Ministry 'Diplomacy and Economy' seminar on the burning of Wenzhou shoes in Elche, Spain, arguing that 'trade is the meat, diplomacy is the bone' and warning of EU technical barriers.
notes: Hurun spelling 'Dongyi' matches 东艺鞋业 (Wenzhou). Leatherbiz Payless item does not name him personally. Very private; no published contacts found.

name: Zhang Hongyu
profile: Listed on the Hurun China Rich List 2005-2008 as Zhang Hongyu (张鸿毓) of Qian Li Ma Group (pharmaceuticals, software, property). No web sources found confirming further details.
notes: No findable online footprint in English or Chinese searches; needs Chinese corporate registry research.

name: Yang Hao
profile: Listed on the Hurun China Rich List (2005) as Yang Hao (杨毫), wealth from Chengdu Zhixin Industrial Group (property). No web sources found confirming further details.
notes: Common name and no online footprint found; only appeared on Hurun 2005. Do not confuse with lawyers or academics named Yang Hao.

name: Suresh Venkatachari
current_role: Chairman & CEO, SecureKloud Technologies Ltd (formerly 8K Miles Software Services), since Feb 2024
profile: Chennai/US-based serial IT entrepreneur who founded 8K Miles Software in 2008 (renamed SecureKloud Technologies), a cloud, security and healthcare-IT services firm; earlier founded SRM Technologies (1999). He also served as CEO of Nasdaq-listed spinoff Healthcare Triangle (2019-2023) and returned as SecureKloud chairman & CEO in 2024.
interesting_fact: Over 35 years in IT services, he has founded several technology companies, three of which went public.
deep_cut_fact: Back in 2011, when 8K Miles was a young cloud startup, he told YourStory that 'security in cloud is one of the biggest concerns' of customers, foreshadowing the company's later rebrand to SecureKloud.
notes: Also known as Suresh V. Chari. Company has had governance/audit controversies in the past; keep outreach focused on cloud/healthcare-IT and data infrastructure.

name: Sameer Padmakar Mulay
current_role: Managing Director, Ajeet Seeds Pvt Ltd (Aurangabad / Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar)
profile: Second-generation head of Ajeet Seeds, one of India's largest cotton-seed companies, founded by his father Padmakar Mulay. Joining when revenue was Rs 18 crore, he grew it to roughly Rs 700 crore by 2015, driven by the Bt cotton hybrid Ajeet 155, and diversified into bajra, corn, wheat, paddy and vegetable seeds.
interesting_fact: The Ajeet 155 Bt cotton hybrid (2006), developed with Mahyco-Monsanto technology, pulled the company back into profit by 2008 and became its breakout product.
deep_cut_fact: He originally aspired to be a civil engineer and join the family construction business, but a 1996 tea-time talk with his father steered him to the College of Agriculture, Pune (graduated 2001) and into seeds.
notes: Private company; corporate general email is the only published route. Agri focus, little energy/data-center angle.

name: Ashok Anand Chandavarkar
current_role: Executive Director, FDC Limited (Mumbai-listed pharmaceutical company)
profile: Member of the Chandavarkar family that controls FDC Ltd (formerly Fairdeal Corporation), the Mumbai drugmaker known for the oral rehydration brand Electral. A mechanical engineer, he joined FDC in 1987, became Executive Director in 1996 and oversees materials procurement, inventories and general management; still listed as an active ED in FDC's April 2026 governance filing.
interesting_fact: FDC traces back to 1936, when founder Anand Chandavarkar began importing infant foods, drugs and surgical appliances; it is today the 'custodian' of Electral, India's best-known oral rehydration salts brand.
deep_cut_fact: Though FDC is a pharma company, he trained as a mechanical engineer (B.E. Mechanical) and is actively involved in running FDC's CSR activities, sitting on its CSR committee.
notes: Born 1941 per NSE filing (age ~85). Low public profile; route via FDC company secretary/IR. Active-director status from NSE integrated governance filing Apr 2026: https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/corporate/ixbrl/INTEGRATED_FILING_GOVERNANCE_151745_21042026113420_iXBRL_WEB.html

name: Venkateswara Prasad Kondragunta
profile: Founder-promoter and managing director of Sandhya Marines, a Visakhapatnam shrimp processor and exporter incorporated in 1987 that sells mostly frozen shrimp to the US, plus subsidiary Aquatica Frozen Foods. The group has expanded into shrimp feed milling. Listed on Hurun India 2019.
interesting_fact: In 2025 Sandhya Marines became the first shrimp feed miller in India certified under the Aquaculture Stewardship Council (ASC) Feed Standard, awarded by DNV at World Aquaculture India 2025.
notes: Very low personal media profile; role from registry aggregators (qorpiq/paperli) only. Company website did not load during research. Also listed as MD of Pinnacle Hospitals India per registry mirrors (unverified).

name: Seth Dallaire
current_role: EVP & Chief Growth Officer, Walmart Inc. (also a director of Shift4 Payments)
profile: Ad-tech and retail-media executive who runs Walmart's global enterprise platforms: Walmart Connect advertising, Walmart+, Walmart Data Ventures, VIZIO, Sam's Club MAP and Marketplace. Previously Walmart U.S. chief revenue officer (2021-24), Instacart CRO, and eight years leading Amazon's global ad sales; earlier at Yahoo and Microsoft. Wealth is from executive equity.
interesting_fact: At Instacart he built the advertising business from the ground up, partnering with more than 2,500 brands, before Walmart hired him to scale its retail-media arm.
deep_cut_fact: A liberal-arts product rather than a typical tech exec: he holds a BA from Vassar College, plus an MBA from NYU.
notes: Data/advertising angle (Walmart Data Ventures, VIZIO) is the strongest hook. Route via Walmart media relations or LinkedIn.

name: Sharon Mates
current_role: Former Chairman & CEO, Intra-Cellular Therapies (acquired by J&J, Apr 2025); director of Medincell and Benitec Biopharma
profile: Biotech founder (PhD, University of Washington) who co-founded Intra-Cellular Therapies in 2002 and led it as chair and CEO through FDA approval of the antipsychotic Caplyta (2019) and its $14.6bn sale to Johnson & Johnson in 2025. Earlier she was president of North American Vaccine and co-founded Functional Genetics. Now sits on biotech boards and speaks on biotech M&A.
interesting_fact: She steered one company from founding to a $14.6bn cash exit in 23 years; J&J paid $132 a share to gain Caplyta for schizophrenia and bipolar depression.
deep_cut_fact: Intra-Cellular was built on Nobel laureate Paul Greengard's prize-winning work on intracellular signalling; she co-founded it with Greengard, Allen Fienberg and Moshe Alafi, and won a 2019 ISCDD leadership award for it.
notes: ITCI is now part of J&J, so no company IR route. Appears on conference circuits (e.g. BIO Investment & Growth Summit, Mar 2026: https://bigs.bio.org/speakers/sharon-mates); Medincell/Benitec board routes possible.

name: R Brad Martin
current_role: Executive Chairman / Chairman of the Board, FedEx Corp (since June 2025); chairman, RBM Venture Company; director, Westrock Coffee
profile: Memphis businessman who led the investor group that bought Proffitt's in 1984 and grew it from a 10-store East Tennessee chain into Saks Incorporated, serving as chairman & CEO 1989-2006. FedEx director since 2011, he became FedEx chairman in June 2025 after founder Fred Smith's death. Runs private investment firm RBM Venture Co.
interesting_fact: He served as interim president of the University of Memphis (July 2013 - May 2014), his alma mater, between running Saks and chairing FedEx.
deep_cut_fact: Before retail, he served five terms in the Tennessee House of Representatives and is described as the youngest person ever elected to the Tennessee legislature.
notes: Also an author with Abingdon Press. Deep-cut source (William & Mary Law page, indexed in search) now returns 404; Vanderbilt Owen profile also places his legislative service in the 1970s.

name: Mark W. Jenkins
current_role: Chief Financial Officer, Carvana Co. (since July 2014)
profile: Carvana's CFO since 2014, recruited by CEO Ernie Garcia III; besides finance he oversees strategic planning, Carvana's lending platform, marketing distribution and the data science behind vehicle acquisition and pricing. He helped steer Carvana's 2023-24 debt restructuring and turnaround to profitability. Wealth is from Carvana equity.
interesting_fact: He told Fortune Carvana's comeback rested on a three-step plan: drive operating efficiency, restore profitability, then return to growth.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining a startup as CFO, he was a Wharton finance professor (2009-14) researching consumer and corporate credit markets, with a Stanford economics PhD and a Duke B.S.E. in mathematics and civil engineering.
notes: Low personal media profile; best route is Carvana communications/IR.

name: Jennifer A Parmentier
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Parker-Hannifin Corp (CEO since Jan 2023, chair since Jan 2024); director, Nordson
profile: Industrial executive leading Parker-Hannifin, the Cleveland-based motion and control technologies maker. She joined Parker in 2008, ran the Sporlan and Hose Products divisions and the Engineered Materials Group, then served as COO before becoming CEO. Earlier career at Ingersoll Rand/Trane Residential and Magna. Wealth is from executive equity.
interesting_fact: She rose from division general manager to COO overseeing all of Parker's operating groups (2021), then became CEO in Jan 2023 and added chair in Jan 2024, succeeding Tom Williams.
deep_cut_fact: One of her early Parker posts was general manager of the Sporlan Division, which makes refrigeration and air-conditioning flow-control valves, before she ran the Hose Products Division.
notes: Parker's aerospace and thermal/filtration lines give a possible energy/data-center angle. Route via Parker IR.
